PART 01 — ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE

AI Industry Headlines

Aug 4 – Aug 6, 2026 · Autonomous Driving · Funding & M&A · Regulation · Infrastructure

01

Waymo Explores $15B+ Funding Round at Near $100B ValuationFUNDING

Alphabet's self-driving unit Waymo is in talks with investors to raise over $15 billion at a valuation approaching $100 billion. The round is led by Dragoneer, with participation from Sequoia, DST Global, and other institutions. This would be one of the largest private financing rounds in transportation tech history, fueling speculation that Waymo may be preparing for an IPO. Waymo currently operates fully driverless robotaxi services in San Francisco, Phoenix, Los Angeles, and other cities.[1]

02

Wayve Secures $1.2B from SoftBank, Nvidia & Uber for Embodied AIEMBODIED AI

UK autonomous driving startup Wayve has completed a $1.2 billion funding round led by SoftBank, with participation from Nvidia, Uber, and three major automakers. The capital will accelerate its "embodied AI" technology — an end-to-end deep learning approach that navigates complex environments without relying on high-definition maps. Wayve's approach stands in sharp contrast to traditional map-based autonomous driving and is considered closer to the path of general intelligent driving.[2]

03

Moove Raises $250M Series C for Autonomous Vehicle InfrastructureROBOTAXI

UAE-based mobility tech company Moove has closed a $250 million Series C funding round, lifting its valuation to $2.1 billion. The new capital will be used to build autonomous driving operational infrastructure, including vehicle maintenance networks, remote takeover centers, and data processing platforms. As the robotaxi industry accelerates toward deployment, specialized infrastructure suppliers are becoming a key bottleneck and investment hotspot.[3]

04

EU AI Act Transparency Provisions Officially Effective August 2REGULATION

The European Commission announced that the core transparency provisions of the Artificial Intelligence Act officially entered into force on August 2. The new rules require interactive AI systems to clearly disclose their AI identity, and AI-generated images, audio, and video deepfakes must be labeled. General-purpose AI models must disclose training data summaries and establish governance systems. Violations can result in fines of up to 6% of global turnover.[4]

05

EU Plans €30B for AI Gigafactories to Catch Up with US & ChinaINFRASTRUCTURE

The European Commission has launched a tender for up to 7 AI "gigafactories," aiming to mobilize approximately €30 billion in combined public and private investment to close Europe's AI computing gap with the US and China. Brussels says it is pursuing a dual track of regulation and investment — enforcing the AI Act on one hand while accelerating compute infrastructure on the other. The gigafactories will provide European AI startups with domestic compute support, reducing reliance on US cloud providers.[5]

06

Anthropic's $15B Data Center Financing Scheme Backed by GoogleINFRASTRUCTURE

Despite a $96.5 billion valuation, Anthropic cannot fund AI compute infrastructure on its own. Its data center project in Hubbard, Texas, uses a $15 billion multi-layer financing structure led by Nexus Data Centers and backstopped by Google's credit — separating the physical data center from internal chips, similar to the Nvidia-OpenAI credit swap model. This signals that the AI era is far more capital-intensive than the internet era.[6]

07

South Korea to Provide Free AI Services to All 52 Million CitizensPUBLIC POLICY

The South Korean government announced it will provide free AI services to all 52 million citizens nationwide, with a beta version launching in September and full rollout by year-end. The government will provide selected companies with up to 512 Nvidia B200 processors, with funding guaranteed through 2030. At least 50% of the system's compute capacity must run on domestically-built AI models meeting government standards. The initiative aims to lower AI adoption barriers, boost digital literacy, and support the domestic AI industry.[7]

08

HappyRobot Raises $150M as Enterprise Agent Sector Heats UpAI AGENTS

Enterprise AI agent startup HappyRobot has closed a $150 million funding round with participation from a16z, BlackRock, and other prominent institutions. The company focuses on building enterprise-grade "agent-as-a-service" software that automates complex cross-system business workflows. This week has seen dense financing activity in the enterprise AI agent space, indicating that B2B AI applications are moving from proof-of-concept into large-scale deployment.[8]

09

Unitree, World's Largest Humanoid Robot Maker, Files for IPO at ~$6.2B ValuationIPO

China's Unitree opens its IPO subscription on August 10 on Shanghai's STAR Market at a ~$6.2 billion valuation. Last year it shipped ~5,500 humanoids, more than any rival, on $237M revenue and 60% margins. For contrast, US rival Figure is valued at $39B with almost no revenue. A pre-IPO perpetual contract is already live on MEXC at ~$72.

10

Physical AI Is Already on Factory Floors and in Homes: 29 Startups MappedPHYSICAL AI

CryptoDiffer published a Physical AI landscape map covering 29 private startups across four categories: humanoids (Figure, 1X), warehouse & construction robots (Bedrock, ANYbotics), self-driving vehicles (Waymo, Waabi), and autonomous defense systems (Anduril, Shield AI). Industrial robotics is the most crowded segment (9 companies), while autonomous vehicles has the fewest players (5), signaling Physical AI has moved from concept to deployment.

PART 02 — WEB3 & BLOCKCHAIN

Web3 & Blockchain Headlines

Aug 4 – Aug 6, 2026 · ETF Flows · Market Data · Regulation · On-Chain

11

Spot Bitcoin ETFs See $244M Net Inflows, Third Consecutive DayETF FLOWS

US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $244.4 million in net inflows in a single day, marking the third consecutive trading session of positive flows. BlackRock's IBIT led with $196.8 million in inflows. Despite ongoing market volatility, institutional investor demand for regulated digital asset exposure continues to recover. Market analysts view this as a signal of institutional capital buying the dip after the recent oversold correction.[9]

12

BTC Rebounds to $64,451, $235M in Short Positions LiquidatedMARKET

Bitcoin price rebounded to $64,451, gaining approximately 2.4% in 24 hours and triggering roughly $235 million in forced short liquidations. Ethereum rose 2.1% in tandem to $1,908. The market saw a technical rebound after the CLARITY Act delay was priced in, but institutional demand remains weak and the upside potential is yet to be confirmed. The Fear & Greed Index remains in the Fear zone.[10]

13

CLARITY Act Delayed Again, Passage Probability Drops to 16%REGULATION

The US Senate has once again delayed consideration of the CLARITY Act for digital asset market structure, and prediction markets now put the probability of it being signed into law this year at just 16%. SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce stated that regulatory reform will continue even if the bill does not pass. The legislative impasse has become the biggest source of uncertainty for crypto markets, as investors reassess the impact of the regulatory timeline on asset pricing.[11]

14

Robinhood Launches $200M VC Fund for Early-Stage Web3 ProjectsVENTURE

Retail brokerage Robinhood announced the launch of a $200 million venture capital fund focused on Y Combinator-stage Web3 early-stage projects. The fund will target DeFi, NFTs, on-chain gaming, and decentralized social sectors. Robinhood aims to build a crypto ecosystem moat, using its portfolio to enhance user engagement and product innovation on its platform.[12]

15

BTC Whale Opens 40x Short on 1,600 BTC, Partially LiquidatedWHALE WATCH

On-chain data monitoring detected a Bitcoin whale opening a 40x leveraged short position of 1,600 BTC (approximately $102 million) at $64,202, with a liquidation price of $65,810. As the price rebounded toward $65,000, 200 BTC of the position was partially liquidated, resulting in a loss of approximately $146,000. The remaining 1,400 BTC short position now has a liquidation price of $64,998. Intense long-short battle is driving elevated short-term volatility risk.[13]

16

Exchange Token Market Cap Rose 10.6% in July, Hit All-Time HighMARKET DATA

In July, the total market capitalization of exchange tokens rose by 10.6% MoM, reaching a new ATH of $33.4B. The increase showed that investor interest in the sector remained resilient despite the broader crypto market's weak performance in 2026. YTD gain stands at 4.5%.

17

CEX Listings Climb Back 20% in July, MEXC Accounts for Nearly HalfMARKET DATA

New CEX listings rose to 98 in July 2026, up 20% MoM from 82 in June, which had been the lowest monthly total in two years. MEXC led with 43 listings (nearly half), followed by Binance at 17 and KuCoin at 9. The recovery signals market回暖 after June's trough.

18

Robinhood Became the Leading Layer 2 Chain by Revenue in JulyL2 DATA

In July, the combined transaction fee revenue of Layer 2 networks reached approximately $6.3M. Robinhood generated $3.5M of that, nearly 56%. Base delivered $2.0M for second place, while Arbitrum managed only $534K. Robinhood's emergence as the primary L2 revenue driver signals a profound shift in the L2 landscape.

19

Exchanges Raised the Most VC Capital in July at $543M, Crypto.com Alone Took $400MVC FLOWS

Exchange topped every crypto VC category at $543M in July, more than double Payments or AI. But that lead comes almost entirely from a single round -- Crypto.com's $400M strategic raise from Citadel Securities. AI projects led by number of rounds with 9, becoming the most active category. Payments ranked second at $244M.

Trend Outlook

This week in AI, the autonomous driving sector has exploded in full force. Waymo's near-$100B valuation raise, Wayve's $1.2B SoftBank-led round, and Moove's $250M Series C — three major funding deals landing in close succession — signal that embodied AI and robotaxi are transitioning from technology validation into large-scale expansion. Combined with continued heat in enterprise agents and AI infrastructure, the AI capex curve shows no sign of inflection.

On the Web3 side, three consecutive days of spot Bitcoin ETF inflows signal institutional dip-buying, but another delay to the CLARITY Act remains a medium-term overhang. Against a backdrop of whale high-leverage shorting and dual long-short liquidations, the short-term market will remain range-bound, with attention focused on whether the $65,000 resistance level can be decisively broken.

Across both sectors, AI compute demand and Web3 on-chain activity are diverging — AI capital expenditure continues to exceed expectations, while crypto markets trade in shrinking volume within a regulatory vacuum. The intersection of these two narratives — AI-driven on-chain security auditing and decentralized compute networks — may represent the next phase of structural opportunity.
